title: PhysicsLENS: Diagnosing Physical Property Blindness in Video Generation Models
title_zh: PhysicsLENS：诊断视频生成模型中的物理属性盲区

paragraphs.en: Reliable video world models could provide scalable predictive environments for robot learning, planning, and evaluation. However, generated robot videos can violate physical principles and complete tasks through physically implausible behavior, limiting their reliability for robot learning and planning. Current video-generation benchmarks exclude physics that are inherently hidden by visuals (e.g., weight, viscosity, friction). Due to this, video models are evaluated on the fidelity of physics, not the underlying accuracy of physics. We introduce PhysicsLENS, a dataset and benchmark for evaluating plausibility of physical properties grounded in robotics. PhysicsLENS uses matched scenario pairs that hold the same conditioning frame and task, while varying underlying physics in the scene description. Scenarios are curated from public robot video sources and annotated across seven physical domains: collision, gravity, momentum, friction, deformation, fluid, and causality. We evaluate across four video generation models, producing over 400 human-annotated labels. Results show that plausible-looking videos often ignore the stated property (34 of 47), and that stating the property lowers plausibility only slightly and not significantly.
paragraphs.zh: 可靠的视频世界模型能够为机器人学习、规划与评估提供可扩展的预测环境。 然而，生成的机器人视频可能违反物理原理，并通过不符合物理规律的行为来完成任务，这限制了其在机器人学习与规划中的可靠性。 目前的视频生成基准测试排除了那些本质上被视觉画面所隐藏的物理属性（例如重量、粘度、摩擦力）。 正因如此，视频模型评测的是物理表现的外观逼真度，而非底层物理的准确性。 我们提出 PhysicsLENS，一个用于评估以机器人为基础的视频物理属性合理性的数据集与基准测试。 PhysicsLENS 采用配对的场景：两者使用相同的条件帧和任务，仅在场景描述中改变底层物理特性。 场景选自公开的机器人视频来源，并标注了七个物理领域：碰撞、重力、动量、摩擦、形变、流体与因果性。 我们对四个视频生成模型进行了评测，生成了超过 400 条人工标注的标签。 结果表明，看起来合理的视频常常忽略了所指定的物理属性（47 个中有 34 个），并且明确说明该属性仅略微降低合理性，且差异并不显著。

paragraphs.en: Video generation models could provide scalable predictive environments for robot learning ( Yang et al., 2024 ; NVIDIA, 2025a ) , planning ( Du et al., 2023 ) , and evaluation ( Quevedo et al., 2025 ) . By generating diverse interactions without repeatedly collecting real-world data, these models could expose robots to rare events, unfamiliar objects, and changing physical conditions ( Jang et al., 2025 ) . However, increasing the volume of generated data is useful only if the videos reliably represent the physical consequences of actions. A video may appear realistic and depict successful task completion while violating friction, momentum, object permanence, or other physical constraints. Such violations undermine the usefulness of generated videos as predictive environments, yet may go undetected by benchmarks focused on visual realism and task success. We therefore require a benchmark that evaluates whether generated interactions respect the physical properties and constraints that govern them.

paragraphs.en: Existing video-generation benchmarks capture this reliability only partially. Most benchmarks focus on visual quality, temporal consistency, or motion plausibility. These criteria can identify obvious artifacts, but cannot determine whether a model correctly grounds the physical properties specified in its conditioning input. Properties such as weight, friction, viscosity, and deformability may not be observable from a single image. Consequently, visually identical scenes can require different outcomes: a robot should interact differently with a heavy object than with a light one, or with a slippery surface than with a rough one. A model can therefore generate a plausible video while producing behavior that is physically incorrect for the stated condition.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的视频生成基准只能部分衡量这种可靠性。 大多数基准关注视觉质量、时间一致性或运动合理性。 这些标准能够识别明显的伪影，但无法判断模型是否正确落实了其条件输入中规定的物理属性。 重量、摩擦力、粘度和可变形性等属性可能无法从单张图像中观察到。 因此，视觉上相同的场景可能需要不同的结果：机器人与重物和轻物的交互方式应当不同，与光滑表面和粗糙表面的交互方式也应当不同。 因此，模型可能生成一段看似合理的视频，同时其行为相对于给定条件而言在物理上是不正确的。

paragraphs.en: We introduce PhysicsLENS, a benchmark for evaluating both physical plausibility and physical-property grounding in robot video generation. The dataset comprises of curated image–text prompts, more than 400 clips generated by four video generation models, and structured human annotations for every clip. We construct prompts from public robot videos, grouping scenarios into seven physical domains: collision, gravity, momentum, friction, deformation, fluid, and causality. In unobservable scenarios, the text specifies a physical property that cannot be inferred from that frame. Matched unobservable prompts keep the visual context and task fixed while varying the specified property, allowing us to test whether generated interactions reflect the corresponding physical consequences. Figure 1 summarizes the benchmark workflow.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 PhysicsLENS，一个用于评估机器人视频生成中物理合理性与物理属性接地能力的基准。 该数据集由精心整理的图像-文本提示、四个视频生成模型生成的 400 多个视频片段，以及每个片段的结构化人工标注组成。 我们从公开的机器人视频构建提示，并将场景归入七个物理领域：碰撞、重力、动量、摩擦、形变、流体和因果性。 在不可观测的场景中，文本指定了无法从该帧推断出的物理属性。 匹配的不可观测提示在保持视觉情境和任务不变的同时改变所指定的属性，从而测试生成的交互是否能反映相应的物理后果。 图 1 总结了该基准的工作流程。

paragraphs.en: The benchmark evaluates generated clips through two complementary tracks. In the human evaluation track, annotators rate physical plausibility and task completion, describe and categorize visible physical violations, and assess whether interactions in unobservable scenarios reflect the stated property. In the automated evaluation track, a four-stage hierarchical pipeline screens each clip, localizes potential violations, verifies them through targeted vision-language model questions, and reports supporting evidence. Across four video-generation models and 439 generated clips, the results show that a video’s apparent physical plausibility does not guarantee correct grounding in a hidden property. Our contributions are:

paragraphs.en: We introduce PhysicsLENS, a robotics-focused benchmark covering seven physical domains and distinguishing physical plausibility from physical-property grounding.
paragraphs.zh: 我们推出 PhysicsLENS，一个以机器人为重点的基准，涵盖七个物理领域，并区分物理合理性与物理属性基础。

paragraphs.en: We construct matched scenarios that preserve visual context while varying text-specified physical conditions, including properties that cannot be inferred from appearance alone.
paragraphs.zh: 我们构建了匹配的场景，这些场景在保留视觉上下文的同时改变由文本指定的物理条件，包括那些无法仅从外观推断的属性。

paragraphs.en: We present a multi-stage evaluation procedure and benchmark four video-generation models with more than 400 human judgments, finding that plausible-looking videos often ignore the stated property.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了一种多阶段评估流程，并对四个视频生成模型进行了超过400次人类评判的基准测试，发现看似合理的视频往往忽略了所声明的属性。

paragraphs.en: Video world models are increasingly used as simulators and data sources for robot learning ( Yang et al., 2024 ; NVIDIA, 2025a ; Jang et al., 2025 ) , yet videos that look realistic can still break physics ( Kang et al., 2025 ; Motamed et al., 2026 ) . Distributional metrics and general benchmark suites mainly measure perceptual quality ( Unterthiner et al., 2018 ; Huang et al., 2024 ) , although VBench-2.0 adds physics dimensions ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . Physics benchmarks score commonsense physics in generated videos ( Bansal et al., 2025 ; Bansal et al., 2026 ; Meng et al., 2025 ; Gu et al., 2026 ) , compare generations with real experiments or recorded outcomes ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Motamed et al., 2026 ) , or turn measured motion into verifiable rewards ( Le et al., 2025 ) . Physion-Eval and PQSG also localize failures, using expert reasoning traces and VLM-generated question graphs, respectively ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Pothiraj et al., 2026 ) . For robotics, WorldSimBench, EWMBench, RBench, and RoboWM-Bench evaluate generated manipulation videos on visual quality, motion, task adherence, or whether the motion can be executed as actions ( Qin et al., 2025 ; Yue et al., 2025 ; Deng et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ) . WorldModelBench scores instruction following and physics adherence across domains that include robotics ( Li et al., 2025 ) , and RoboGaze reports temporally localized glitches under a robotics-specific taxonomy ( Nguyen et al., 2026 ) . To our knowledge, none of these benchmarks separates properties that are visible in the conditioning frame from properties stated only in the prompt (Table 1 ), so a high score cannot show whether a model followed the stated physics or only what the scene looks like.

sents.zh: 在机器人领域，WorldSimBench、EWMBench、RBench 和 RoboWM-Bench 从视觉质量、运动、任务遵循程度或运动能否被执行为动作等方面评估生成的操作视频（Qin et al., 2025；Yue et al., 2025；Deng et al., 2026；Jiang et al., 2026）。

sents.en: WorldModelBench scores instruction following and physics adherence across domains that include robotics ( Li et al., 2025 ) , and RoboGaze reports temporally localized glitches under a robotics-specific taxonomy ( Nguyen et al., 2026 ) .
sents.zh: WorldModelBench 在包括机器人在内的多个领域对指令遵循和物理一致性进行评分（Li et al., 2025），而 RoboGaze 依据机器人专用分类体系报告时间上可定位的故障（Nguyen et al., 2026）。

sents.en: To our knowledge, none of these benchmarks separates properties that are visible in the conditioning frame from properties stated only in the prompt (Table 1 ), so a high score cannot show whether a model followed the stated physics or only what the scene looks like.
sents.zh: 据我们所知，这些基准均未将条件帧中可见的属性与仅在提示词中声明的属性区分开来（表 1），因此高分无法表明模型是遵循了所声明的物理规律，还是仅仅遵循了场景的外观。

paragraphs.en: Inferring properties that appearance does not reveal is a classic test of physical understanding: Physion++ and ComPhy ask models to infer mass, friction, elasticity, or charge from observed interactions ( Tung et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2022 ) . PhysicsLENS reverses this flow of information: the property is stated in text, and the generator must turn it into motion. Controllable generators receive physical quantities as dedicated inputs, such as forces or mass and friction coefficients ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Gillman et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2026 ) . T2V-CompBench tests whether prompt attributes bind to the right objects, but only for visible attributes such as color, shape, and motion direction ( Sun et al., 2025 ) . We instead test whether general-purpose image-to-video models follow a property given only in plain language, with the frame and task held fixed.
paragraphs.zh: 推断外观无法揭示的属性是物理理解的经典测试：Physion++ 和 ComPhy 要求模型从观察到的交互中推断质量、摩擦力、弹性或电荷（Tung et al., 2023；Chen et al., 2022）。 PhysicsLENS 颠倒了这一信息流向：属性以文本形式给出，生成器必须将其转化为运动。 可控生成器将物理量作为专用输入接收，例如力或质量与摩擦系数（Liu et al., 2024；Gillman et al., 2025；Li et al., 2026）。 T2V-CompBench 测试提示词属性是否绑定到正确的对象，但仅限于颜色、形状和运动方向等可见属性（Sun et al., 2025）。 我们则测试通用图像到视频模型是否遵循仅以普通语言给出的属性，同时保持帧和任务固定不变。

paragraphs.en: Automatic physics evaluation often relies on vision-language models (VLMs), either fine-tuned or prompted ( Bansal et al., 2025 ; Meng et al., 2025 ; NVIDIA, 2025b ) , but their reliability is limited. VLMs struggle with physical-world understanding ( Chow et al., 2025 ) , most models score near chance on intuitive-physics tests ( Bordes et al., 2025 ) , and plausible verbal explanations can hide wrong estimates of velocity and acceleration ( Puyin et al., 2026 ) . Multimodal judges also show biases and inconsistent judgments ( Chen et al., 2024 ) , and video VLMs have limited fine-grained motion and temporal grounding ( Hong et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) . Measured evidence helps: MASS adds depth, object grounding, and motion tracking to VLM reasoning ( Wu et al., 2026 ) , and GeoPhys finds that VLM judges detect physics violations near chance while a training-free score on frozen image-encoder features does better ( Internò et al., 2026 ) . PhysicsLENS follows this direction by combining tracked measurements with targeted VLM questions, and we test it directly against human annotations.
paragraphs.zh: 自动物理评估通常依赖视觉语言模型（VLM），无论是经过微调的还是通过提示驱动的（ Bansal et al., 2025 ; Meng et al., 2025 ; NVIDIA, 2025b ），但它们的可靠性有限。 VLM 在物理世界理解方面存在困难（ Chow et al., 2025 ），大多数模型在直觉物理测试中的得分接近随机水平（ Bordes et al., 2025 ），而且看似合理的语言解释可能掩盖对速度和加速度的错误估计（ Puyin et al., 2026 ）。 多模态裁判还存在偏差和判断不一致的问题（ Chen et al., 2024 ），并且视频 VLM 在细粒度运动和时间定位方面的能力有限（ Hong et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ）。 实测证据会有所帮助：MASS 在 VLM 推理中加入了深度、物体定位和运动跟踪（ Wu et al., 2026 ），GeoPhys 发现 VLM 裁判检测物理违规的能力接近随机水平，而在冻结的图像编码器特征上使用免训练的分数则表现更好（ Internò et al., 2026 ）。 PhysicsLENS 沿着这一方向，将跟踪测量与针对性的 VLM 问题相结合，我们直接将其与人工标注进行了对比测试。

paragraphs.en: Image-conditioned video generation relies on two sources of information: an initial frame and a text prompt describing the scene and requested task. In ordinary robot videos, visual appearance is often correlated with physical properties; for example, size may correlate with mass, and visible wetness may suggest low surface friction. A model may therefore generate plausible motion from visual priors without grounding the physical properties specified in text. PhysicsLENS evaluates whether models follow text-specified properties when those properties cannot be inferred from the initial frame. We define two conditions. In the observable condition, the prompt is consistent with the physical properties suggested by the frame. In the unobservable condition, the same frame is paired with a prompt that specifies a latent property that departs from those visual expectations. For example, a prompt may state that liquid inside an ordinary teapot is “thick and viscous, similar to molasses” (Figure 2 ). A model that relies only on appearance may instead generate water-like flow. We refer to this failure to condition on a text-specified latent property as physical property blindness .
paragraphs.zh: 图像条件视频生成依赖两类信息：一帧初始画面和一个描述场景与所要求任务的文本提示。 在普通的机器人视频中，视觉外观往往与物理属性相关；例如，尺寸可能与质量相关，可见的湿润可能暗示表面摩擦较低。 因此，模型可能仅凭视觉先验生成看似合理的运动，而未将文本中指定的物理属性落实到位。 PhysicsLENS 评估的是：当某些物理属性无法从初始帧推断出来时，模型是否会遵循文本中指定的这些属性。 我们定义了两种条件。 在可观测条件中，提示与该帧所暗示的物理属性相一致。 在不可观测条件中，同一帧画面与一个提示配对，该提示指定了一个偏离上述视觉预期的潜在属性。 例如，提示可能声明普通茶壶内的液体“浓稠而黏滞，类似糖浆”（图 2）。 仅依赖外观的模型反而可能生成类似水的流动。 我们将这种未能以文本指定的潜在属性为条件的现象称为物理属性盲视（physical property blindness）。

paragraphs.en: Each unobservable scenario is derived from an observable counterpart with the same initial frame and task instruction. Only the scene description changes: the observable description is consistent with the frame, whereas the unobservable description introduces a latent property that conflicts with its visual appearance. This construction holds the visual scene, task, and frame quality fixed, making the textual property the sole intervention. Because we generate only one video per prompt and model, individual pairwise differences may reflect generation noise; we therefore analyze matched pairs in aggregate. The unobservable scenarios specify four task-relevant properties: viscosity for pouring (10 scenarios), surface condition for wiping (8), elasticity for deformable objects (7), and mass for pushing (5). Each property is expressed in plain language within the scene description provided to the video generator. The generator receives neither a reference continuation nor the expected outcome.
paragraphs.zh: 每个不可观测场景都由一个具有相同初始帧和任务指令的可观测对应场景推导而来。 只有场景描述发生变化：可观测描述与帧一致，而不可观测描述引入了一个与其视觉外观相冲突的潜在属性。 这种构建方式将视觉场景、任务和帧质量保持不变，使文本属性成为唯一的干预因素。 由于每个提示词和模型只生成一个视频，单对配对差异可能反映生成噪声；因此我们对匹配对进行汇总分析。 不可观测场景指定了四类与任务相关的属性：倾倒相关的粘度（10个场景）、擦拭相关的表面状况（8个）、可变形物体相关的弹性（7个）以及推动相关的质量（5个）。 每个属性都以通俗语言表达在提供给视频生成器的场景描述中。 生成器既不会收到参考续写内容，也不会收到预期结果。

paragraphs.en: The design supports two complementary evaluations. Property grounding assesses whether the generated video visibly reflects the stated latent property, using the human adherence score (Section 3.3 ). Matched-condition comparison tests whether specifying that property affects physical plausibility while holding the initial frame and task fixed—that is, whether failure to express the property coincides with visibly less plausible physics. Together, these evaluations distinguish general visual plausibility from adherence to the specified physical condition.
paragraphs.zh: 该设计支持两项互补的评估。 属性落地评估生成的视频是否在视觉上体现出所声明的潜在属性，使用人类依从度评分（第 3.3 节）。 匹配条件对比测试在固定初始帧和任务的前提下，指定该属性是否会影响物理合理性——也就是说，未能表现出该属性是否与视觉上明显较低的物理合理性同时出现。 这两项评估结合在一起，可以区分一般视觉合理性与对指定物理条件的依从。

paragraphs.en: PhysicsLENS contains 110 prompts: 80 observable scenarios and 30 matched unobservable variants. The 80 starting frames come from 11 public robot datasets that cover humanoids, dual-arm and single-arm manipulators, and mobile manipulators (Table 6 ). Each frame shows the scene before the robot interacts with solid objects or liquids. Appendices A and B describe frame preparation, prompt generation, and the annotation schema. We used GPT-4o to draft structured scene and action descriptions from each frame and its logged task. An author subsequently reviewed the descriptions.

paragraphs.en: We generate one video per prompt using each of four models: Wan 2.2 ( Team Wan et al., 2025 ) , Cosmos 3 Nano ( Agarwal et al., 2026 ) , HunyuanVideo 1.5 ( Wu et al., 2025a ) , and MAGI 4.5B Distill ( Teng et al., 2025 ) . Together, they span diverse generative paradigms, including diffusion video models, autoregressive video generation, and world/action foundation modeling. One unobservable HunyuanVideo 1.5 prompt did not produce a usable video. The realized benchmark hence contains 439 videos: 320 observable and 119 unobservable. HunyuanVideo 1.5 contributes 109 videos, including 29 unobservable videos, while each other model contributes 110. paragraphs.en: PhysicsLENS also includes an automated evaluator (Figure 3 ). paragraphs.en: The evaluator has four stages. Screening measures motion over the first 5 seconds of the video: frame differences, optical flow, camera motion, flow-direction entropy, and how DINOv2 frame embeddings change. It also asks a VLM a physics-error question that lists specific errors instead of asking about overall realism. Localization tracks points with camera motion removed and measures their kinematics: speed, acceleration, the time of peak acceleration, and points that disappear inside the frame rather than at its border, the sign of an object vanishing mid-video. VLM verification shows each VLM eight frames and the task and asks three questions: (i) whether the task was completed; (ii) which of eight failure descriptions (one per physical domain, plus an object appearing or vanishing) best describes the main physics problem, if any; and (iii) for unobservable scenarios, whether the outcome shows the stated property. Reporting merges the evidence into a per-video JSON report with each finding’s time window, object, violation type, confidence, and a short explanation. We do not evaluate time localization because our human labels are not time-dependent. The released tool also runs per-domain specialists in Stage 3, which our experiments do not use (Appendix C ).

paragraphs.en: To compare with human ratings (Section 4.4 ), we pose these questions to ten VLMs and read each answer from the probabilities of its first output token. paragraphs.en: This section presents results on the PhysicsLENS benchmark and evaluates its diagnostic pipeline through four research questions. RQ1–RQ3 are answered with human annotations, and RQ4 compares the pipeline against them. RQ1: Does high physical plausibility imply that a model followed a grounded specification (Sec. 4.1 )? RQ2: Does stating a latent property in text change plausibility (Sec. 4.2 )? RQ3: What do individual failure cases reveal about the distinction between grounding and plausibility (Sec. 4.3 )? RQ4: Can the PhysicsLENS pipeline approximate human judgments (Sec. 4.4 )?
paragraphs.zh: 本节介绍 PhysicsLENS 基准的测试结果，并通过四个研究问题评估其诊断流程。 RQ1–RQ3 通过人工标注来回答，RQ4 则将该流程与人工标注进行对比。 RQ1：高物理合理性是否意味着模型遵循了有依据的规范（第 4.1 节）？ RQ2：在文本中陈述某个潜在属性是否会改变合理性（第 4.2 节）？ RQ3：个别失败案例能揭示「有依据」与「合理性」之间的何种区别（第 4.3 节）？ RQ4：PhysicsLENS 流程能否近似人类判断（第 4.4 节）？

paragraphs.en: Fig. 6 illustrates why a plausibility rating alone cannot establish property grounding. In a task that specifies molasses-like tea, all four generators produce plausible pours that fail to reflect its viscosity ( H = 1 H{=}1 ). Wan 2.2, for example, pours the tea like water while receiving the highest plausibility rating (Fig. 6 a). A different case arises when the requested interaction barely occurs. MAGI’s robot often remains nearly still (Fig. 6 c), producing a video that looks plausible without demonstrating how the stated property affects the task.
paragraphs.zh: 图 6 说明了为什么仅凭合理性评分无法确立属性落地。 在一个指定糖浆状茶水的任务中，所有四个生成器都产生了看似合理却未能反映其粘性的倾倒（H = 1 H{=}1）。 例如，Wan 2.2 像倒水一样倾倒茶水，同时却获得了最高的合理性评分（图 6 a）。 当所请求的交互几乎不发生时，会出现另一种情况。 MAGI 的机器人常常几乎保持不动（图 6 c），产生的视频看起来合理，却没有展示所述属性如何影响任务。

paragraphs.en: On the contrary, a video can reflect the stated property while violating other physical constraints. With a silicone-coated, liquid-repellent table, HunyuanVideo 1.5 receives an adherence rating of H = 3 H{=}3 , but the glass moves without contact, making the video implausible (Fig. 6 b). In another case, Wan 2.2 leaves an extremely heavy tape dispenser stationary ( H = 4 H{=}4 ), but the robot’s hand passes through it ( P = 1 P{=}1 ). paragraphs.en: PhysicsLENS provides human annotations for 439 videos, allowing us to measure how well automated scores agree with human judgments. We evaluate ten open-weight VLMs from seven families, Stage-1/2 video signals, and combinations of the two. Combination weights and signal selection are fitted using five-fold cross-validation, with all versions of a scenario kept in the same fold. We report AUC, where 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect ranking.
paragraphs.zh: PhysicsLENS 为 439 个视频提供了人工标注，使我们能够衡量自动评分与人类判断的一致程度。 我们评估了来自七个系列的十个开源权重 VLM、Stage-1/2 视频信号，以及两者的组合。 组合权重与信号选择通过五折交叉验证进行拟合，同一场景的所有版本都保留在同一折中。 我们报告 AUC，其中 0.5 表示随机水平，1 表示完美排序。

paragraphs.en: Combining VLM judgments with video signals improves agreement. The full evaluator combines answers from an ensemble of ten VLMs with Stage-1/2 signals. It reaches an AUC of 0.72 for overall plausibility, 0.81 for task completion, 0.73 for violation detection, and 0.71 for hidden-property adherence (Table 4 ). It achieves the highest or tied-highest score on five of the seven measures. Adding signals to an individual VLM raises mean overall plausibility AUC from 0.53 to 0.61, violation detection from 0.58 to 0.72, task completion from 0.71 to 0.76, and property adherence from 0.57 to 0.70. Signals alone reach 0.70 for violation detection; one frequently selected signal tracks objects vanishing during a video.
paragraphs.zh: 将VLM的判断与视频信号相结合可提升一致性。 完整的评估器将十个VLM的集成答案与第一阶段/第二阶段信号相结合。 它在整体合理性方面达到0.72的AUC，在任务完成方面为0.81，在违规检测方面为0.73，在隐藏属性遵循方面为0.71（表4）。 它在七项指标中的五项上取得最高或并列最高的分数。 为单个VLM添加信号后，平均整体合理性AUC从0.53提升到0.61，违规检测从0.58提升到0.72，任务完成从0.71提升到0.76，属性遵循从0.57提升到0.70。 仅使用信号在违规检测上即可达到0.70；其中一个被频繁选中的信号用于追踪视频中物体消失的情况。

paragraphs.en: Generator identity is a strong baseline because the four generators differ substantially in quality. It slightly exceeds the full evaluator on unobservable-video plausibility (0.72 versus 0.71), but assigns the same score to every video from a given generator. Its within-generator AUC is therefore 0.5 by construction, whereas the automated evaluator reaches 0.67 for unobservable plausibility and 0.76 for task completion. Generator identity also cannot score videos from a new generator without first obtaining human ratings for that generator.
paragraphs.zh: 生成器身份是一个强基线，因为四个生成器在质量上差异很大。 在不可观测视频合理性上它略高于完整评估器（0.72 对 0.71），但它对来自同一生成器的每个视频都给出相同的分数。 因此其生成器内 AUC 按构造为 0.5，而自动评估器在不可观测合理性上达到 0.67，在任务完成上达到 0.76。 生成器身份也无法对新生成器的视频打分，除非先获得针对该生成器的人工评分。

paragraphs.en: Targeted questions improve VLM plausibility judgments. When asked directly whether a video is physically plausible, many VLMs perform near chance (Table 5 ). To focus their judgments on physical behavior, we instead ask about specific errors, such as objects passing through one another, vanishing, floating, changing shape impossibly, or moving without contact. The question also instructs the VLMs to disregard task success and the amount of motion. paragraphs.en: We introduced PhysicsLENS, a benchmark for testing whether generated robot videos actually reflect the physical properties they are told to have. By keeping the initial frame and action the same and only changing how the property is described, matched scenarios let us look at property grounding and physical plausibility side by side. Across 439 clips from four generators, human evaluation found a clear gap between the two: 34 of 47 clips rated plausible under unobservable conditions did not follow the stated property, and 15 of 28 clips that did follow it were still physically implausible. In other words, a video can look right without actually respecting the physics it was asked to show, or get the property right while breaking something else entirely. Pairing targeted VLM questions with measured video signals meaningfully improves agreement with these human judgments, reaching an AUC of 0.72 for plausibility and 0.81 for task completion, though judging whether a specific hidden property was followed, and figuring out which physics family a violation belongs to, are both still hard problems. Taken together, these results make the case for evaluating plausibility and property grounding as two separate questions, not one.

paragraphs.en: We took each conditioning frame from before the target manipulation and standardized the supplied frames to 1280 × 720 1280\times 720 pixels. paragraphs.en: Collision and Friction scenarios were comparatively easy to source, reflecting the prevalence of pick-and-place and surface-manipulation footage. paragraphs.en: Scenarios were curated from public robotics video sources rather than authored domain-first, and each scenario was subsequently annotated with its governing physical domain by manual review of its action and outcome. This annotation was performed independently of the taxonomy’s construction to avoid circularity: the seven domains were fixed in advance from the tool’s seven specialists (Section 3.4 ), and each scenario was assigned to the domain its physics most directly tests, rather than domains being defined post hoc to fit whatever scenarios happened to be available.

paragraphs.en: The observable/unobservable axis introduced in § 3.1 is orthogonal to domain: a scenario’s domain label is fixed by the physical law under test, while its observability condition determines whether the property governing that law is visually apparent or text-specified. Both matched members of an observable/unobservable pair therefore carry the same domain label.

paragraphs.en: Stage 1 measures motion over the first 5 s of each video, sampled at 8 frames per second in grayscale with the longer side resized to 320 pixels. It computes the mean absolute difference between consecutive frames; dense optical flow ( Farnebäck, 2003 ) ; camera motion, taken as the median flow vector of each frame pair; object motion, the flow left after subtracting camera motion; and the entropy of object-motion directions over the fastest-moving 10% of pixels. It also embeds the eight VLM frames (below) with DINOv2 ( Oquab et al., 2024 ) and measures how the embedding moves: the step size between frames, how that step size changes, whether successive steps keep their direction, and net displacement relative to path length. Each measurement is reduced to one number per video (a mean, 95th percentile, maximum, or ratio), giving 22 screening signals. No signal is thresholded into a flag. Signals become scores only when evidence is combined, by ranking videos against each other (below). Stage 1 also asks the VLM the physics-error question (Table 10 ). It asks the model to count specific physics errors (objects passing through each other, appearing or vanishing, floating, changing shape impossibly, or moving untouched) and to ignore task success and the amount of motion.
paragraphs.zh: 阶段 1 度量每个视频前 5 秒内的运动，以每秒 8 帧的采样率在灰度下进行采样，并将较长边缩放至 320 像素。 它计算连续帧之间的平均绝对差值；稠密光流（Farnebäck, 2003）；相机运动，取自每对帧的中位光流向量；物体运动，即从光流中减去相机运动后剩余的部分；以及运动最快的 10% 像素在物体运动方向上的熵。 它还使用 DINOv2（Oquab et al., 2024）对八帧 VLM 帧（见下文）进行嵌入，并度量嵌入的移动情况：帧与帧之间的步长、该步长的变化、连续步长是否保持方向，以及相对路径长度的净位移。 每项度量都被归约为每个视频的一个数值（均值、第 95 百分位数、最大值或比值），从而得到 22 个筛选信号。 没有任何信号会被设置阈值而转化为标记。 只有当证据被组合起来、通过视频之间的相互排序（见下文）时，信号才会转化为分数。 阶段 1 还会向 VLM 提出物理错误问题（表 10）。 它要求模型统计具体的物理错误（物体相互穿透、凭空出现或消失、悬浮、以不可能的方式改变形状，或在未被接触的情况下移动），并要求模型忽略任务是否成功以及运动量的大小。

In the interactive tool, Stage 2 goes further. A VLM names the objects, SAM 3 ( Carion et al., 2026 ) segments and tracks them, Stage-1 flags are grouped into time windows, and each constraint family is ranked with a confidence and a time window. paragraphs.en: Stage 4 writes a JSON report for each video from the shared evidence store. The report holds a chronological timeline of findings, each with its time window, object, violation type, confidence and the specialist’s explanation, together with the Stage-2 family ranking and each tool’s severity. An optional text LLM summarizes the report in prose. Stage 4 adds no score of its own. In the interactive tool, routing happens between Stages 2 and 3: only the specialists that Stage 2 ranks highest (three by default) run on a video. paragraphs.en: To test whether the physics-error question helps outside robot videos, we compare it with the standard question on VideoPhy-2 ( Bansal et al., 2026 ) . We use 1,200 videos from its test split, sampled evenly across the seven generators and the five physical-commonsense ratings. We count a video as plausible when its human physical-commonsense score is at least 4 and as implausible when it is at most 2, and drop the 274 videos rated 3, which leaves 926 videos (541 plausible, 385 implausible). We ask Qwen3-VL-32B, Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B both questions with the same frame sampling and answer scoring as above, and compare the two AUCs with a paired DeLong test. Qwen3-VL-32B improves from 0.645 to 0.720 ( p < 10 − 6 p<10^{-6} ), Qwen3-VL-8B from 0.666 to 0.708 ( p = 0.006 p=0.006 ), and Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 0.581 to 0.655 ( p < 0.001 p<0.001 ).
